questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I chose Bologna because I have family in Italy. I have lived in Denmark my entire life, but I thought it would be interesting to experience Italian culture in a different way than just as a tourist. With my program at the University of Copenhagen, I only had two options in Italy: Bologna and Milan. I chose Bologna because it is a smaller city, where I felt I could have the most authentic experience.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I think it has been difficult to navigate both from the University of Copenhagen's side and from the University of Bologna. There is a lot of information, various emails, and very little communication between the two universities. I have missed having clearer communication from both sides.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I haven't really received any assistance as such. I registered my arrival through a somewhat complicated online system, where it was only possible to proceed at specific times. I think it would have worked better if I could have shown up in person. All I had to do was show my flight ticket, receive some brief information, and then I could ask questions.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: We found a landlord who rented out apartments to many people in Bologna.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: They should know that it is a very good idea to have this arranged before arriving in the city. Additionally, one can try to talk to people who have been in the city before and get contact information for landlords. Through our network, we found a landlord who rented out apartments to many people in Bologna.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I registered my arrival through a somewhat complicated online system, where it was only possible to proceed at specific times. I think it would have worked better if I could have shown up in person. All I had to do was show my flight ticket, receive some brief information, and then I could ask questions.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Only online help was available. We tried to get in touch with different people at various offices in Bologna, but found it very difficult. They all referred us to the online help desk.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: We have been very confused about the courses. We were informed very late that we had to take at least 50% of our courses in humanities, as that is the faculty we are affiliated with in Copenhagen. On the other hand, it was easier to change courses in Bologna than in Copenhagen. In fact, we could change courses up until November. This was because some courses did not require physical attendance or only started in mid-November. Furthermore, the process of getting courses approved (pre-approval) at KU and the Online Learning Agreement is quite complicated. Each time we changed a course, the process had to start over, which was very frustrating.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I would advise other prospective exchange students to choose courses based on their own faculty and to get as many courses pre-approved as possible in advance – to avoid having to go through the lengthy process later.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level in Bologna was not very high in my courses, but the teaching was enjoyable, and it also provided an opportunity to learn more about Italian culture.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teachers were a bit slower and somewhat lazier compared to what I experience at KU.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Applied Political Sociology 
Introduction to Italian Culture 
Visualizing the Italian Society 
Education Systems and Politics 
Social Studies of Science and Technology

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Visualizing the Italian Society – It was fun to watch older Italian films and have them combined with some history. The teacher's English was poor, but it was manageable.

Education Systems and Politics – Very interesting, especially if you're studying sociology.

Social Studies of Science and Technology – Very similar to a course one could take in Denmark. The instructor was skilled, and the exercises and assignments were well-designed.

questions.answer: ESN Bologna

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Explore the city on foot.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Visit the San Luca Church – very beautiful.
Wine tasting.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Bologna is a city known for its university, so many exchange students automatically come here, especially for the English-taught courses I was enrolled in. Therefore, I found it quite easy to adapt.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer:
Go to Via Del Pratello and have a drink and a chat with the local students 
Be in the city before all of the other exchange students arrive

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer:
The language 
The food 
The people

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Don't stress about the courses and the system there – everything will work out in the end, and the university is willing to help.
Choose courses with exams that don't require you to return to Bologna if you fail.
Make sure to sort out your housing situation in good time.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I definitely think the most rewarding part was experiencing the Italian culture up close.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The biggest challenge was probably that I lived very close to my roommates. We were four people in a very small apartment, and it can be demanding to make that work. Additionally, I also felt there were significant challenges with their entire system and the communication with the people from the university who were supposed to help us. However, in the end, there was a solution to it.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
